schema_note: Mirrors TTB's benchmark-config.v3 SHAPE and is consumed by this repo's runner. It is deliberately NOT claimed to be a valid v3 document: it has never been validated by TTB's backend, and `execution.agent` here is an external agent process rather than TTB's `agent_loop.rs`. Validating against the real schema is the upstream-port step.

dataset.provenance: the resolved_ids of litellm+qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-t0 on a neutral 50, scored by the official grader on the OpenHands branch
dataset.note: A DEBUGGING INSTRUMENT, not a resolve rate: on instances this model family has already solved, a zero is attributable to the stack. It is model-specific by construction — valid for Coder-30B, meaningless for a weaker model.
dataset.prompt_source: run_swebench.py PROMPT constant (NOT a pinned dataset snapshot — this set has no snapshot, so the prompt is not version-pinned here)

agent.note: opencode owns its own system prompt, plan discipline and tool set. TTB's agent stanza (system_prompt / user_prompt_template) does not apply: layering a second workflow over a black-box CLI would measure the emulation rather than the agent. Both arms restart the server per instance; asymmetric restarts produced a flattering number here once already.

decoder.note: Both arms serve this same file. Not a TTB-registered model: TTB's configs/models has no Coder-30B entry, so there is no upstream pin to match and no TTB row to compare against.

max_wall_time_s.mechanism: subprocess timeout in run_swebench.py; on expiry whatever the agent has written to disk is still captured and graded

max_agent_steps.reason: opencode exposes no step cap (`opencode run --help`: no such flag). Declared null rather than aspirationally — TTB's own H1 audit is a config declaring max_steps: 1 while runs used a hardcoded 64.

max_model_calls.reason: not exposed by opencode; measured after the fact from opencode's session store instead of bounded

max_output_tokens.scope: per model call, not per run
max_output_tokens.mechanism: `limit.output` in integrations/opencode/opencode.json; there is no run-level token budget

harness.dataset_name_note: Verified, because KNOWN_SOLVABLE_BOTH is defined over Verified.
harness.note: TTB pins its scorer as an image DIGEST (sslee0cs/ttb-swe-bench-scorer@sha256:ca4bd811...). This profile runs the official harness locally; the analogous pinning is images/digests.json, written by pin_images.sh from what was actually pulled. `:latest` is not reproducible and is not used for a recorded run.
harness.images_note: images/digests.json pins all 31 grader images present: the 20 for this lite-20 set plus the 11 for the Verified known-solvable set used elsewhere in this repo. pin_images.sh verify passes. Re-pin only deliberately — a silent change there changes what a recorded number means.

reporting.telemetry_source: opencode.db (agent-side accounting: tokens_input/tokens_output/assistant-message count per directory-scoped session)
